chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from ʿAlī ibn Hassan, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام regarding His, the Exalted's, saying:
He is the One Who sent down the Book to you; in it are decisive verses—they are the Mother of the Book.
He said: “Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام and the Imams.”
Then as for those in whose hearts is deviation—
Their companions and the people of their wilayah.
So they follow that of it which is allegorical, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation; and none knows its interpretation except Allah and those firmly rooted in knowledge.
Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام and the Imams عليهم السلام.

key_terms.آيَاتٌ مُحْكَمَاتٌ: decisive verses whose meaning is established and foundational
key_terms.الْفِتْنَةِ: discord, trial, or misguiding confusion sought through misuse of scripture
key_terms.زَيْغٌ: deviation or perversity in the heart
key_terms.مُتَشَابِهَاتٌ: allegorical verses susceptible to misreading by those without proper authority
key_terms.وَلَايَتِهِمْ: their wilayah, meaning loyal affiliation and authority

ai.seo_question: Who are the ones firmly rooted in knowledge in Qur'an 3:7 according to Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a tafsir of the verse of muhkamat and mutashabihat by identifying the firmly grounded authorities in divine knowledge with Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام and the Imams عليهم السلام. It also contrasts them with people of deviation who pursue allegorical passages for fitnah and self-directed interpretation, highlighting wilayah and rightful religious authority.
